---
title: "baler.toml"
---

A `{box}`-`{baler}` module needs one metadata file: `baler.toml`. It sits at the root of the module project, one level above the source directory, and declares identity, dependencies, and (optionally) compiled code. It can contain up to five tables:

| Table | Required | Purpose |
|--------------------|----------------------------|-------------------------|
| `[project]` | yes | Module identity and source location |
| `[dependencies]` | no | Runtime R package and baler-module dependencies |
| `[extras]` | no | Dev-only dependencies (test frameworks, mocks) and external tools and Python packages (doc generators, linters, Python libraries) |
| `[compiled-code]` | no | Location(s) of compiled code, build-time-only package deps, and what `baler bundle` ships |
| `[tool.test]` | no | Test framework configuration (currently advisory only) |

## `[project]`

This block defines the authorship of the module, and this block is always required. As what the table below said, this contains the info of the author of `{box}`-`{baler}` module library:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|-----------------|-----------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| `name` | string | yes | Module name. Also the default source-directory name when `src` is omitted. |
| `version` | string | yes | Strict semver (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`). Parsed when the file loads; a malformed version fails there, not later inside whoever depends on this module. Dependency ranges (`^`, `>=`, etc.) in another module's `[dependencies.baler]` entry resolve against it. |
| `description` | string | yes | May be empty. |
| `authors` | array | yes | See [Authors](#authors) below. |
| `license` | string | yes | SPDX identifier or free-form text. |
| `r_version` | string | yes | Minimum R version (e.g. `">=4.0.0"`). See note below. |
| `readme` | string | no | Path to a README file. |
| `repository` | string | no | |
| `keywords` | array of strings | no | Defaults to empty. |
| `src` | string | no | Path to the source directory, relative to the project root. Defaults to a directory named exactly `name`. The chosen directory *must* contain `__init__.r` or `__init__.R`. |

::: {.callout-note title="Technical Notes"}
-  `r_version` is enforced against the R installation on `PATH`, at both `baler install` and `baler lock` time. A mismatch fails loudly rather than letting a module load under an R it wasn't declared compatible with.

-  Both `__init__.r` and `__init__.R` are accepted (case-insensitive entry-point detection). This matches `{box}` module's internal behaviour.
:::

### Authors {#authors}

Each entry is either a plain string or an inline table:

``` toml
authors = [
    "Jane Doe",
    { name = "Joshua Marie", email = "joshua.marie.k@gmail.com", url = "https://joshuamarie.com", orcid = "0000-0000-0000-0000" },
]
```

Inline-table fields:

| Field   | Required | Notes                               |
|---------|----------|-------------------------------------|
| `name`  | yes      | Display name                        |
| `email` | no       |                                      |
| `url`   | no       | Personal or organisational homepage |
| `orcid` | no       | ORCID iD                            |

## `[dependencies]`

Runtime dependencies, both R packages and other baler modules, live in the same top-level table (a sibling of `[project]`, not nested under it):

- A bare key is an R package, resolved off CRAN (or a custom `repo`). This is the equivalent of `Imports` in an R package's `DESCRIPTION`.
- A nested `[dependencies.baler]` table holds other baler modules this module depends on.

``` toml
[dependencies]
dplyr = "*"
ggplot2 = ">=3.4.0"
fable = { version = "*", repo = "https://tidyverts.r-universe.dev/" }

[dependencies.baler]
other_module = { git = "https://github.com/<user>/<repo>", tag = "v1.2.0" }
utils = { git = "https://github.com/<user>/<repo>", branch = "main", module_dir = "utils" }
```

A bare string value works the same as a table with only `version` set: the `repo` used is the default mirror, `https://cloud.r-project.org`.

::: {.callout-note title="Technical Notes"}
Because module deps and package deps share one table, told apart by whether an entry sits under the reserved `baler` key rather than by any `type`/`mode` field, an R package literally named `baler` cannot be declared as a bare key here.
:::

### Version-spec syntax

Version requirements follow `Cargo.toml`-style syntax, always written as strings:

| Syntax              | Meaning                                  |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `"*"`               | Any version                              |
| `">=1.0.0"`         | Lower bound only                         |
| `">=1.0.0, <2.0.0"` | Inclusive range (comma-separated bounds) |
| `"^1.2.0"`          | SemVer-compatible with 1.2.0             |
| `"=1.2.3"`          | Exact pin                                |

CRAN version strings that use dashes (e.g. `4.0-3`) are normalised to dots before parsing.

### Module dependencies: `git` and `url`

A `[dependencies.baler]` entry names where the module comes from, using the same keys `baler install` takes as flags:

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | no | Constraint string, e.g. `"^1.0"`. Defaults to `"*"` when omitted. Still checked against the fetched module's own declared `version`. |
| `git` | one of `git` / `url` | A `https://github.com/...` repository URL. Only `github.com` URLs are supported, the same as `baler install --git`. |
| `branch`, `tag`, `rev` | no | At most one of these, and only together with `git`. Selects a specific ref to fetch. |
| `module_dir` | no | Directory inside the `git` repo that holds the module, for a repo holding more than one. Only valid with `git`. |
| `url` | one of `git` / `url` | A direct link to an already-bundled `.tar.gz`, e.g. a GitHub Release asset produced by `baler bundle`. |

``` toml
[dependencies.baler]
helpers = { git = "https://github.com/user/repo", tag = "v1.2.0", module_dir = "helpers" }
tools = { url = "https://github.com/user/repo/releases/download/v1.0.0/tools_1.0.0.tar.gz" }
core = "^2.0"    # bare string: registry lookup, not implemented yet
```

Exactly one of `git` or `url` may be set. Setting both, or setting `branch`/`tag`/`rev`/`module_dir` without `git`, fails to load `baler.toml` immediately, before any resolution or fetch is attempted. Unknown keys (a typo such as `tga`) are rejected the same way, rather than being silently ignored.

A bare-string entry, or a table with only `version` set, parses fine but has no source to resolve against, since there's no default module registry yet:

``` toml
[dependencies.baler]
other_module = "*"   # will fail at resolution time, no registry yet
```

## Extra dependencies for development 

`[extras]`, by default, has the same shape as `[dependencies]`, bare keys for R packages, a nested `.baler` table for baler modules, except dependencies under this block are only needed during development (a test framework, a mock module), not at runtime. It also has one thing `[dependencies]` doesn't: `[extras.external]`, for non-R tools and Python packages. Here's an example: 

``` toml
[extras]
testthat = "*"
covr = "*"
# rlang = "*"

[extras.baler]
# mock_module = { url = "https://github.com/user/repo/archive/refs/tags/vX.Y.Z.tar.gz" }
# utils = { git = "https://github.com/<user>/<utils>" }
```

### External development tools

Under `[extras.external]` block, you can declare anything a module's development needs that isn't a traditional R package or a `box-bale` module: a command-line tool such as Quarto, or a Python package. `{baler}` never fetches or installs any of it, it only checks for it and reports. Each entry picks its kind with `type` (two, as of now):

1.  `cli`: A command binary name on `PATH`. The declared tools under this type are checked through running `<tool> --version`. 

2.  `python`: A Python distribution name (strictly on this sense, so for the `{sklean}` library instance, it should be written as `scikit-learn`, not `sklearn`). The declared packages are checked by reading the package's installed version from one Python interpreter. 

Here's an example:

``` toml
[extras.external]
pandoc = ">=3.0"            # a bare string is a `cli` entry

[extras.external.quarto]
type = "cli"                # the default when `type` is left out
version = ">=1.4"
hint = "https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/"

[extras.external.numpy]
type = "python"
version = ">=1.24,<3"

[extras.external.internal-stats]
type = "python"
version = ">=2.0"
index = "https://pypi.internal.example/simple"
```

#### `cli` entries

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | yes | A requirement in the same syntax as [Version-spec syntax](#version-spec-syntax) above. |
| `hint` | no | Printed when the tool is missing, e.g. a download page. |

The key must be a bare command name. A path separator is rejected when `baler.toml` loads. The version is read from the first dotted number in the tool's `--version` output (`3.1` is read as `3.1.0`). A tool that prints its version some other way is reported as unreadable, not as a mismatch. Messages include the path of the tool that was checked.

#### `python` entries

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | yes | A [PEP 440](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/) specifier such as `>=1.24,<2` or `~=1.24`. This is *not* the Cargo-style syntax used elsewhere in this file, but it is the same string `pip` accepts. |
| `python` | no | Interpreter to check, instead of the automatically resolved one. A bare name is looked up on `PATH`, anything with a path separator is used as given. |
| `index` | no | A private package index URL. Only changes the install hint. |
| `git` | no | A git URL. Only changes the install hint. Cannot be combined with `index`. |

All `python` entries are checked in one interpreter run, so which interpreter is used matters. It is the first of:

1.  The entry's own `python` field.
2.  `RETICULATE_PYTHON`, since that is the interpreter R's `{reticulate}` will use.
3.  An active `VIRTUAL_ENV` or `CONDA_PREFIX`.
4.  `python3`, then `python`, on `PATH`.

An explicit setting (1 or 2) that doesn't resolve is reported as an error instead of quietly falling through to a different interpreter. Versions are read from package metadata, so checking a package never imports it.

Every message names the interpreter that was checked, and a missing or outdated package comes with an install hint that targets that same interpreter, for example `/home/me/.venv/bin/python -m pip install "numpy>=1.24"`. `index` and `git` only change the wording of that hint, since detection doesn't depend on where a package came from.

#### Checking

`baler compile` and a `--path` install (installing straight from a project directory) check the root project's entries and print a note for anything missing or out of range. This is informational only: it never fails the command. A `--git`, `--url`, or registry install skips this check entirely, since those fetch something closer to a finished release than a project someone is actively developing. A fetched module's own `[extras.external]` is never checked, because checking runs external programs.

Entries are validated when `baler.toml` loads. These fail immediately:

-   An unknown `type`, or an unknown key in an entry (a typo such as `hnit`).
-   `python`, `index`, or `git` on a `cli` entry, or `hint` on a `python` entry.
-   `index` and `git` on the same entry.
-   A `cli` key that is not a bare command name, or a `python` key that is not a valid distribution name.

## Configuration for handling native compiled codes

The `[compiled-code]` block is not always required, until there exist codes written in native languages which requires compilation. In this block, you declare where a module's compiled code lives, any build-time-only R packages whose headers `Makevars` / `R CMD SHLIB` needs (most commonly `Rcpp` or `cpp11`), and what `baler bundle` ships.

``` toml
[compiled-code]
path = "cpp/"                 # single directory, relative to the module's source dir
# path = ["cpp/", "extra/"]   # or an array, for multiple directories

build_deps = { Rcpp = "*" }   # installed before compilation; not a runtime dependency
binary = true                 # `baler bundle` compiles and ships the binary
keep_source = false           # only with binary = true: also ship native source
```

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|-----------------|-----------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| `path` | string or array of strings | no | Directory, or directories, containing native sources + `Makevars`. Relative to the module's own source directory (the same base `src` uses), not the project root `baler.toml` lives in. A single location can be written as a plain string; more than one as an array. |
| `build_deps` | table | no | Map of package name -> version requirement (same syntax as `[dependencies]`). These are resolved and installed **before** `R CMD SHLIB` runs. They do **not** become runtime dependencies; list them again under `[dependencies]` if the compiled code also needs them loaded at runtime. |
| `binary` | boolean | no | Defaults to `false`. When `true`, `baler bundle` compiles the native code in place first and ships the compiled `.lib/` in the archive, without the native source. See [Bundle settings](#bundle-settings). |
| `keep_source` | boolean | no | Defaults to `false`. Only valid together with `binary = true`. Also ships the native source next to the compiled binary. |

### Bundle settings {#bundle-settings}

The `binary` and `keep_source` options describe what the module ships, so they live with the module instead of being retyped on every run. The flags no longer exist, and passing one is now a command-line error. The following table below summarizes the result when those options clash each other: 

| `binary` | `keep_source` | The result of the archive |
|---|---|---|
| `false` (default) | `false` (default) | R source and native code source, no compiled binary. Compiled code is built on install. |
| `true` | `false` | Compiled `.lib/` binary, native source left out. |
| `true` | `true` | Compiled `.lib/` binary and native source. |
| `false` | `true` | Rejected when `baler.toml` loads: `keep_source` needs `binary = true`. |

If `binary = true` but the module has no native code, `baler bundle` prints a warning and bundles without a binary. A binary bundle only works reliably on the platform and R version it was built for, see [Binary bundles](native-code.qmd#binary-bundles).

### Resolution rules

1.  If `path` is set, those directories (relative to the module's source dir) are used, whether written as a single string or an array. 
2.  Otherwise, `{baler}` scans the whole module source tree for directories that contain a `Makevars` (or recognised C/C++ sources). This is the behaviour you get when `[compiled-code]` is omitted entirely. 

The directory name itself is free (`c/`, `cpp/`, `fortran/`, `src/`, ...); detection is driven by the presence of build artefacts, not by a fixed folder name. See also the scaffolding produced by `baler init --native`.

::: {.callout-note title="Technical Notes"}
-   FORTRAN scaffolding is recognised by the language parser but not yet supported by the build pipeline (`R CMD SHLIB` is only invoked for `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cc`/`.cxx` sources). 
-   Compiled shared objects are placed in `<module>/.lib/` (next to `__init__.R`) so that `box::file()` resolves them correctly.
-   Build results are cached by source hash + R platform + R version.
:::

## Unit Testing

Under `[tool.test]` block, advisory configuration for a future test runner. As of now, `{baler}` does not yet execute tests.

| Field       | Type   | Required | Notes                                              |
|-------------|--------|----------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `framework` | string | yes      | e.g. `"testthat"`                                  |
| `dir`       | string | yes      | Directory containing tests (auto-detected when `"__tests__"`) is used |

## Full template

This is the exact text written by `baler init`. `[compiled-code]` is only included at all when `--native` is passed; a plain `baler init` leaves it out entirely rather than writing a commented-out placeholder for it.

``` toml
[project]
name = "convert"
version = "0.1.0"
description = ""
authors = [
    { name = "Your Name", email = "you@example.com" },
]
license = "Unknown"
r_version = ">=4.0.0"
repository = ""
keywords = []
# readme = "README.md"
# src = "convert"    # path to the source directory containing __init__.R
                    # defaults to a directory named after the module

[dependencies]
# dplyr = "*"
# ggplot2 = ">=3.4.0"
# fable = { version = "*", repo = "https://tidyverts.r-universe.dev/" }

[dependencies.baler]
# A module needs a source: `git` (a github.com repo) or `url` (a
# bundled .tar.gz). `git` can take one of branch/tag/rev, and
# module_dir for a repo holding more than one module. `version` is
# optional.
# other_module = { git = "https://github.com/user/repo", tag = "v1.0.0" }

# [extras]/[extras.baler] hold deps only needed outside normal
# runtime use (tests, mocks, dev tooling), same shape as
# [dependencies]/[dependencies.baler] above. [extras.external] adds
# one more kind found only here: external CLI tools, never loaded by
# box, so never part of [dependencies] at all.
[extras]
# testthat = "*"

[extras.baler]
# mock_module = { git = "https://github.com/user/repo" }

[extras.external]
# baler doesn't install these, only checks for them. A bare string is
# a version spec; an inline table can carry whatever else that
# particular tool needs, since baler itself only reads `version`.
# quarto = ">=1.4"

# [tool.test]
# framework = "testthat"
# dir = "tests"
```

When `baler init --native cpp` (or `--native c`, etc.) is used, a `[compiled-code]` block is added, populated with the appropriate `path` and `build_deps` for the chosen language / backend:

``` toml
[compiled-code]
# Native code is auto-detected under this module's source dir, no
# path needed for the default src/ layout. Only set path if compiled
# code lives somewhere else, or in more than one place.
# path = "native/"
# path can also be an array: path = ["native/", "extra/src"]
build_deps = { Rcpp = "*" }
# build_deps is resolved and installed before compiling.
# Does not imply a runtime dependency; list it in
# [dependencies] too if the compiled code also needs it
# loaded at runtime
```
